correctness.rationale: For any fixed full-dimensional convex polygon with genuine interior angles α_i∈(0,π), every-sided sampled event has complement probability ≤Σ_i(1−d_i/P)^N. On that event the missing perimeter is exactly Σ_i [a_i+b_i−sqrt(a_i²+b_i²−2 a_i b_i cosα_i)]. Multivariate nearest-gap survival gives independent Exp(1) limits for N a_i/P and N b_i/P, while exponential endpoint tails and the exponentially rare empty-side event yield convergence of all fixed integer moments. Substitution S=U+V~Gamma(2,1), T=U/S~Uniform gives one-corner MGF ∫(1−z bα(t))^−2 dt, b=1−sqrt(1−4cos²(α/2)t(1−t)). Its first singularity is zα=1/(1−sin(α/2)) and exact local blow-up exponent −3/2 from a nondegenerate quadratic maximum. Independent numerical quadrature at α=π/2 and deltas 10^-3, 10^-5 gave normalized constants 1.0007845895 and 1.0000080797. Product singularity locates smallest angle; its exponent determines multiplicity; analytic factor division and induction recover every angle. Checker source inspected, but numerical quadrature is not used for the universal theorem.

value.rationale: Recoverability of the complete unordered angle multiset from one natural asymptotic stochastic observable is a meaningful inverse-geometric classification across all convex polygons. The result also sharply shows that side lengths and congruence class are unidentifiable, so its scope has an informative boundary beyond trivial normalization.

limitations: Only fixed convex polygons, independent uniform arclength sampling, ideal full limiting distribution.
No edge lengths, vertex order, congruence, finite-N inverse rate or stability.
An earlier perimeter-specific Laplace inverse theorem or identifiability of angle-dependent convolution factors may exist under different terminology.
